description:
What the OWOX Data Marts Open Exchange Rates connector loads: historical exchange rates, one row per day, base currency and target currency, in one table. For each day in the requested range the connector calls the historical endpoint and writes the `rates` object it returns as one row per currency.

All rates on a row are relative to one unit of its `base` currency (US dollars unless another base is set, which Open Exchange Rates allows only on its Developer, Enterprise and Unlimited plans). There is nothing to join: the table carries no key that points at another table. Join it to your own data on `date` and the currency code.
questions: What was one US dollar worth in euros on each day of the last year?
Which currencies changed the most against the base currency over the last 30 days?
How would last quarter's orders look converted to a single currency at the rate of each order's date?

Historical exchange rates data.description:
Historical exchange rates: one row per `date`, `base` currency and target `currency`, with the `rate` of one unit of the base in that currency. The base is repeated on every row because it can be changed, so a table loaded with several bases keeps them apart.

Open Exchange Rates publishes the last value of each UTC day; a request for today's date returns the most recent rate rather than an end-of-day value. Which currencies are loaded depends on the symbols the connector is configured with.
questions: What was the rate between the base currency and a given currency on each day of a month?
Which currency had the largest percentage change against the base over the last quarter?
What was the average monthly rate for each currency over the last year?
